prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active peptide forms of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep B046 as a single-part prize with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 did not merely repeat the opening unanimity: every member re-argued the case on its content, and the substance holds. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and insulinotropic action in humans, Drucker defined proglucagon processing, receptor biology and the wider actions of the peptide, and Mojsov is credited with identifying and synthesising the active truncated peptide. These findings were independently confirmed for decades and then converted into a drug class with randomized outcome evidence in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints. Maturity is high and the clinical effect is already large. The citation names the physiology and active peptide forms and the therapies that followed, without naming a product, which keeps it a prize for discovery.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point and the round-1 exchange did not remove it. Mojsov's priority on GLP-1(7-36) is contested, Habener is outside the credited names, and I cannot settle that dispute from the supplied evidence. Leaving out Knudsen means the long-acting analogues that carried most patient benefit are recognised only through the citation wording, which a critic can call incomplete. Against this, replacing Mojsov with Knudsen would turn a physiology prize into a drug-development prize, and leaving Mojsov out on an unverified priority claim would be a substantive judgement without documentary support. A one-part prize also leaves CAR-T unrecognised this year, and long-term safety of obesity indications is still accumulating, which is a data-accrual point and not a reason to wait.

responses.point: Perlmann keeps Mojsov over Knudsen, arguing that the prize recognizes the discovery that changed the field and not the best-executed drug programme, and that Knudsen would be named only if the committee decides the achievement is drug development.
responses.response: Your argument persuades me and is the main reason I have moved off my opening Drucker-Holst-Knudsen set. The peptide-identification step is a necessary link and a contested priority does not erase a contribution. I accept your conditional: Knudsen belongs on the ballot only if the committee rewrites the citation around the medicines, and I do not think the supplied evidence compels that. I keep the citation free of any product name and let the 'made possible incretin-based therapies' clause carry the translational consequence. I do not agree, however, that the dispute can be left as a footnote. If it cannot be documented, the citation should name the peptide forms modestly.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would rather cite the physiological discovery and name the peptide chemistry modestly than omit Mojsov on an unverified claim, and would pair CAR-T with GLP-1 only if the committee wants a two-part prize.
responses.response: I agree with your handling of the priority question: omitting Mojsov on an unverified claim would be the larger error, and the modest wording 'active peptide forms' reflects that. On CAR-T, you answer the question I raised in the chair's summary about a pairing. Any second part requires dropping one of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov under the three-person cap, and your own reasoning says none of the three should go. A two-part prize would also leave CAR-T with Eshhar outside the credited names. I therefore do not move to a two-part configuration, although I share your view that CAR-T is the strongest second achievement.

responses.point: Sandberg says that substituting Knudsen for Mojsov moves the citation from discovery to drug design, but that Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is a coherent alternative that Sandberg would not oppose on the science if a majority prefers a development-inclusive prize.
responses.response: Your statement is fair to my earlier proposal, and I accept that the coherence of Drucker, Holst and Knudsen does not make it the better choice here. Knudsen's work on half-life extension is a real scientific achievement, but it builds on an established mechanism, and Mojsov's contribution defines what the active hormone is. I share your wish that the committee check the priority record before finalising. Because we cannot do that from the evidence supplied, I treat the Drucker-Holst-Mojsov trio as the position consistent with what is documented. On second achievements I still place B007 below B028, since its treated population is narrow and the SMN1 gene discovery lies outside the credited pair.

responses.point: Linnarsson regards CAR-T as the strongest challenger and is open to it alongside GLP-1, while recognising that Eshhar is missing from the credited list and that Rosenberg's role is broader than the CAR design.
responses.response: I agree that CAR-T is the strongest challenger and I keep B028 as my first alternative with June and Sadelain only, because Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer is a different achievement from the engineered receptor. I still find the Eshhar omission serious: it bears on whether June and Sadelain can be called the originators, and a two-name credit would need a citation built around clinical translation of CAR designs. That is a harder attribution problem than the GLP-1 one, where the trio is internally coherent. This is why I do not give up a B046 name to open a second part now.

responses.point: El Manira cites the unfolded protein response (B011) with Walter and Mori as a compact, mature credit and notes that long-term safety of obesity indications is still accumulating.
responses.response: On B011 we still agree that Walter and Mori are a compact, very mature credit, and I keep it as my second alternative because its disease-level translation lags the conceptual impact. On safety, I read your point as one about data accrual. Randomized outcome data in cardiovascular and renal endpoints are mature enough that I would not delay a B046 citation, but I would avoid wording that claims settled long-term safety for obesity.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Habener has the stronger documented claim on the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, which I cannot settle from the supplied text.
Whether the committee prefers a citation centred on physiology or on drug development; if the latter, Knudsen would need to be reconsidered and the citation rewritten.
Whether CAR-T (B028) could form a second part if the Eshhar omission and Rosenberg's scope were resolved, since it would require dropping one B046 name.
Whether the long-term safety record for obesity indications should affect the wording of the B046 citation.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal ground is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted ballot. I disclose, as background, about twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1; the count is not independently audited) and a postdoctoral link to Paul Greengard. Neither is a credited name on any shortlisted ballot. Round 1 revealed no new relationship.
